title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1RC1RA_0LD1RB_1LE1LD_1RF0LA_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1RC1RA_0LD1RB_1LE1LD_1RF0LA_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is always an alternating block (10)^x next to a solid block 1^y, and the machine moves cells between them by doubling, back and forth. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; an exact macro simulator finds no halt in the first 1015 steps. Lean proves the left phase rule (below) for all sizes.

What Lean proves. The whole phase map, every case for all sizes (E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, R(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y C>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, k, t) = (10)^m 1 A>0 0 (10)^k 1^t), and halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from R(0, 2), which the blank tape reaches in 2 steps,, reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By native_decide the first 108 phases (about 4.1·1021 machine steps) do not. Lean also proves that the even phases lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape, and checks, for every all-ones tape of length n < 105, that its run halts before the next even phase or all-ones tape exactly when n is 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …). lean/Fatal.lean proves that list for every n, by the kernel (ones_fatal_all, ones_safe_all), and lean/Ones.lean puts this together (halt_needs_ones, strong induction on the number of phases): the machine halts from blank tape if and only if its run reaches an all-ones tape of fatal length. What is not proved: that the run never lands on a fatal length.

Where a halt would come from. F0 halts, and F is entered only from E0: E stands on the 0 at the left end and walks right with F over 0101…, so a halt needs at most one 1 after the alternating block. Probing every two-block tape with sizes below 150, a parity rule keeps that from happening except right after the tape has become all ones; from 1^n C>0 it halts for n = 20, 50, 112, 238 (n = 32·2k − 2k − 12) and for 15 values of n below 40 (all n ≤ 400 checked).

Why it has not halted. All-ones moments are rare: in the first 109 steps the tape was 1^n C>0 at n = 2, 5, 10, 71, 279, 466, 763 and 3002, and between 109 and 1015 steps only at n = 5882, 10234, 12114, 24455, 37818, 48395, 53042 and 405563. None is in the list. The machine very probably never halts, but nothing here proves it.

The recurrence, in closed form (24 November 2026). Lean proves (lean/Doubling.lean) that at its left and right stops the run is the doubling map s ↦ 2s mod L, with a modulus L that grows by 2 a stop; the all-ones tapes of the fatal parity reached from a stop come only from its midpoint 2s = L + 2, and have length L − 4. A halt needs that midpoint exactly when L = 32·2k − 2k − 8 (the only other source of all-ones tapes, an all-ones tape straight after another one, gives lengths that are never fatal, checked for n < 3·105). A residue search on the whole phase map (moduli up to 48, and 2-adic up to 256) finds no congruence that rules this out, and in the doubling coordinates there can be none.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,148 cells have been visited and 3,758 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.334). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.342).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: The exact macro simulator c/mrun.c (blocks of 2 cells, run-length coded, a run crossed at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with) runs 1015 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The two phase rules, along the run
claims.text: Write E(x,z) for E>0 (10)^x 1^z and C(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y C>0 (blank around). In the first 109 steps every left phase with z ≥ 2x+8 went E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) (502 times) and every right phase with 2x ≥ y+6 went C(x,y) → C(x−⌊y/2⌋−2, 2y+5) (490 times).

claims.title: The left phase rule, for all sizes
claims.text: Lean proves, with rfl steps, the crossing lemmas and induction on the number of bounces, that E(x,z) reaches E(2x+4, z−2x−6) whenever x ≥ 1 and z ≥ 2x + 7 (ephase). The phase is a start piece, one bounce (10)^(m+1) 1 A>0 0 (1010)^j 1^(r+3) to (10)^m 1 A>0 0 (1010)^(j+1) 1^(r+1) per copy of 10, and an end piece, generated by py/gen_rules.py: the proof of 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE, whose state D plays the part of A here. The right phase and the parity analysis are not proved.

claims.title: Step counts of the phases
claims.text: From probes: the left phase takes 4x²+24x+30 steps, the right phase y²+6y+7 (y even) or y²+4y+5 (y odd). Doubling costs the square of the block, so the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>.

claims.title: Halting needs an all-ones tape from a sparse list
claims.text: From every two-block tape with x, y, z < 150 the next one was computed. E(x,z) with z even ≥ 2 and C(x,y) with x ≥ 1, y odd lead only to tapes of the same kind or to an all-ones tape 1^n C>0, never to a halt; the machine halts only from E(x,0) and E(x,1). From 1^n C>0 the run goes to E(0, n+1) and then E(4, n−5); the alternating block grows 4, 12, 28, 60, … (x ↦ 2x+4), and the run halts when the ones run out leaving exactly one: n = 20, 50, 112, 238, … = 32·2k − 2k − 12. For n ≤ 37 there are 15 more fatal values (1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 16, 18, 21, 22, 24, 29, 30, 31, 34, 37). All n ≤ 400 checked directly; proved for all sizes in Lean since (the parity classes, the fatal lengths for every n and halt_needs_ones, below).

claims.title: All-ones moments so far
claims.text: In the first 109 steps the tape is 1^n C>0 at n = 2, 5, 10, 71, 279, 466, 763, 3002 (the last at step 372,886,607). Between 109 and 1015 steps, from the exact macro simulation (which sees the moment 1^n <D just after): n = 5882, 10234, 12114, 24455, 37818, 48395, 53042, 405563, at steps about 2.90·109, 1.48·1010, 2.48·1010, 2.06·1011, 7.55·1011, 1.58·1012, 2.09·1012 and 9.26·1014. None is in the list (its members near them: 8164, 16354, 32736, 65502, 524248).

claims.title: The whole phase map
claims.text: Write E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, R(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y C>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, k, t) = (10)^m 1 A>0 0 (10)^k 1^t. next sends each of them to the next one the machine reaches (bounces taken all at once), with 18 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters (one symbolic run of lean/Pieces.lean each, generated by py/pieces.py, and induction for the bounces). next fails only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), which halt (e_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1)
claims.text: halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from R(0, 2), which the blank tape reaches in 2 steps, is E(x, z) with z ≤ 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined and none is E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By the step counts of the pieces (py/phasemap.py run) that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps.

claims.title: The parity classes
claims.text: even_next: the even phases (E(x, z) with z even and z ≥ 2, R(x, y) with x ≥ 1 and y odd, Q(m, k, t) with t even) lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape. So from an even phase the machine cannot halt before the tape is next all ones (even_safe).

claims.title: The fatal all-ones lengths below 10<sup>5</sup>
claims.text: fatal_list, by native_decide: for every n < 105, the run from the all-ones tape R(0, n) = 1^n C>0 reaches a halting phase before an even phase or another all-ones tape exactly when n is 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …) (ones_fatal, ones_safe). For every n it is proved by the kernel in lean/Fatal.lean.

claims.title: The fatal all-ones lengths, for every n
claims.text: ones_fatal_all: for every n with n = 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 for some k, the machine halts from the all-ones tape R(0, n). ones_safe_all: for every other n, any iterate of next from R(0, n) that halts comes after another all-ones tape. The proof: from E(x, z) with z odd the run is a chain of doublings E(x, z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) that halts exactly when z = zHalt(x, k) (e_out, strong induction), with zHalt(x, k) closed-form (zHalt_closed).

claims.title: A halt needs an all-ones tape of fatal length
claims.text: halt_needs_ones: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from R(0, 2), which the blank tape reaches in 2 steps, is an all-ones tape R(0, n) with n fatal (n = 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …)). halt_passes_ones says the same in machine steps: a halting run passes through the configuration R(0, n) for a fatal n. The proof is a strong induction on the number of phases: by ones_safe_all a halt after a non-fatal all-ones tape comes after a later all-ones tape, so the last all-ones tape before the halt is fatal; conversely a fatal one halts (ones_fate).

claims.title: All-ones moments in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: Iterating the map with the pieces' step counts (py/phasemap.py run 100000000): after n = 405563 (step 9.26·1014) the tape is all ones at n = 454194, 469239, 2163591, 10123515, 10839355, 10989362, 14932875, 15458727, 20193339 and 23796235 (the last near step 1.87·1020). None is fatal.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> phases
claims.text: The phase map next of lean/Phases.lean, transcribed into C (tools/c/doubling_phases.c, checked against py/phasemap.py on the first 300,000 phases), iterated 1011 phases from blank tape: no phase e x 0 or e x 1, about 4.1·1030 machine steps; 4 further all-ones tapes after the Lean bound, none fatal (16 November 2026).

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.16·10<sup>23</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 2)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 2 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 2,239,000,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 600 seconds. That is more than 8.16·1023 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: At its stops the phase map is the doubling map s ↦ 2s mod L
claims.text: At a left stop E(x, z) (z even) put s = z + 2, L = 2x + z + 8; at a right stop R(x, y) (y odd) put s = y + 5, L = 2x + y + 7. From every stop except the few below the next stop, one to three phases on, is again a stop, with L′ = L + 2 and s′ = 2s if 2s ≤ L, s′ = 2s − L otherwise (doubling, all sizes). The exceptions: the low end, s = 4 (E(x, 2), which goes to R(x, 3): s′ = 8 = 2s, but L stays) (low), and the midpoint 2s = L + 2, where the next stop is the all-ones tape of even length L − 4 (mid_ones). The all-ones tapes of the other parity, the safe one, come from 2s = L inside the map. So the recurrence behind the all-ones lengths, in closed form, is the doubling map with a modulus that grows by 2 a stop; 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1RA1LC_0RB1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE, 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1LA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE, 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE run the same map with other offsets.

claims.title: No congruence keeps the run off the fatal list
claims.text: The residue search of the doubling-map trio, on the whole phase map: for every modulus N from 2 to 48 and for N = 64, 96, 128, 192 and 256, the phase map taken mod N (every branch the residues allow, both halves of every bounce count) is run to a closed set of classes from the start; in every case some reachable all-ones class is a fatal length mod N. In the coordinates (s, L) there can be none: the two branches s ↦ 2s and s ↦ 2s − L, with L ↦ L + 2, reach every pair of residues of the right parity mod every N ≤ 64. What keeps the run off the list is only which branch is taken, that is the size of s, not a residue (24 November 2026).

claims.title: The chance of a halt from here on
claims.text: Leaving aside the relay lengths, whose targets are never fatal, a halt needs the midpoint 2s = L + 2 at a stop whose modulus is L = 32·2<sup>k</sup> − 2k − 8 (then L − 4 is a fatal length); those moduli double from one to the next. If s sits at a random place below L, the midpoint at a given stop has chance about 1/L, so the expected number of midpoint all-ones tapes up to modulus L is about ½ ln L: 7.1 for the first 20,000,000 phases (L up to 13,300,000), against 10 seen. The chance of ever reaching a fatal one beyond the 10<sup>11</sup> phases already run (L about 6.7·10<sup>10</sup>) is about the sum of 1/L over the fatal moduli above it, below 10<sup>−10</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Lean proves that it halts if and only if the run reaches an all-ones tape whose length is in an explicit sparse list (halt_needs_ones); nothing rules out that the run hits one.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the mechanism is clear. The tape is an alternating block next to a solid block; the machine doubles one at the other's expense, back and forth. It can halt only right after the tape becomes all ones, and only if the number of ones is in a sparse list (20, 50, 112, 238, …, or a few small values).

facts.text: No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 2).
No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases of the phase map proved in Lean (about 4.1·10<sup>21</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the phase map, iterated from the start, reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1).
It halts if and only if its run reaches an all-ones tape of fatal length: n = 0, 6 or 32·2<sup>k</sup> − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …).
At its stops the phase map is s ↦ 2s mod L, L ↦ L + 2; from a stop, the fatal-parity all-ones tapes come only from 2s = L + 2.
No halt in an exact macro simulation (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed at once).
The tape is an alternating block and a solid block; each phase doubles one of them.
From an all-ones tape it halts for n = 20, 50, 112, 238 and some n < 40 (checked to n = 400).
E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6), proved in Lean for all sizes.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,148 cells visited.

sections.heading: Two blocks, doubling
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell and the tape is always an alternating block 10 10 10 … followed by a solid block of 1s. With a for 10, around step 4.8·107:

At the right end the solid block doubles (630 to 1266), eating the alternating block; when that no longer fits, the head goes to the left end and the alternating block doubles instead (119, 238, 480), eating the solid one. Writing E(x,z) for E>0 (10)^x 1^z and C(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y C>0:

• left phase: E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) while z ≥ 2x+8, in 4x²+24x+30 steps: the head bounces between the blocks, each bounce moving one 10 across;
  • right phase: C(x,y) → C(x−⌊y/2⌋−2, 2y+5) while it fits, in about y² steps.

A doubling of a block of size x costs about x² steps and the tape grows by a few cells per phase change, so a tape of width w takes about w³ steps: the width grows like the cube root of time. The split point moves like the doubling map x ↦ 2x on a circle, a textbook chaotic map.

sections.heading: Halting needs an exact landing
html: F reading 0 halts, and F is entered only from E reading 0; E and F together walk right over 0101…. So the run halts only from E>0 (10)^x or E>0 (10)^x 1: a left phase that uses up the solid block leaving exactly one 1.

Parity prevents that in the normal course of things: probing all two-block tapes with sizes below 150, if z is even in the left phase and y is odd in the right phase, the next two-block tape is again of that kind or the tape becomes all ones. From 1^n C>0 the left phase restarts at E(4, n−5); the alternating block goes 4, 12, 28, 60, …, using 14, 30, 62, … ones, and the run halts if exactly one is left: n = 20, 50, 112, 238, 496, … (n = 32·2k − 2k − 12), besides 15 values below 40 (every n ≤ 400 checked).

All-ones moments are rare: n = 2, 5, 10, 71, 279, 466, 763, 3002 in the first 109 steps, and only 5882, 10234, 12114, 24455, 37818, 48395, 53042 and 405563 between 109 and 1015. None was in the list. A crude model (a phase change hits an exact value with chance about 1/width) makes such moments rarer and rarer, and each must also land on a list whose members double: the machine very probably never halts. A proof would have to control the exact remainders of a doubling map.
The same mechanism, with other fatal lists, runs in 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE and its two near-duplicates.

sections.heading: A doubling map with a growing circle
html: Look at the run only at its stops: the left phases E(x, z) with z even and the right phases R(x, y) with y odd. Give each stop a position s and a circle length L: s = z + 2, L = 2x + z + 8 on the left, s = y + 5, L = 2x + y + 7 on the right. Then, at every stop except the few named below, the next stop has
L′ = L + 2,   s′ = 2s if 2s ≤ L,   s′ = 2s − L otherwise,

which is the doubling map s ↦ 2s mod L on a circle that grows by 2 cells a stop (doubling in lean/Doubling.lean, for all sizes). Whether the next stop is on the left or the right is decided by the branch: doubling without wrapping lands on the right, wrapping lands on the left. Each point below is one stop of the run from blank tape (stops 50,000 on): it sits on one of the two dashed lines.

The two exceptions are the ends of the circle. At the low end, s = 4 (E(x, 2), which goes to R(x, 3): s′ = 8 = 2s, but L stays) (low). At the midpoint 2s = L + 2 (the vertical line at 1/2) the next stop is an all-ones tape of even length L − 4 (mid_ones): that is the only way a stop leads to an all-ones tape of the fatal parity, and after it a few phases run off the stops before the map resumes. Those few phases can make another all-ones tape straight away, for a sparse list of lengths (4 → 8, 18 → 24, 48 → 56, 110 → 120, …: the even targets are 2j − 8 (j ≥ 4), never fatal, since 2j − 8 = 32·2k − 2k − 12 has no solution; checked for n < 3·105). All-ones tapes of the other parity come from 2s = L and are ordinary stops.

So the machine halts only if the doubling map hits its midpoint exactly at a stop with L = 32·2k − 2k − 8, one stop out of a list that doubles. Unrolled, sj = 2js0 − Σ εi2j−1−iLi with Li = L0 + 2i and εi the wrap bits: the itinerary is a binary expansion, as chaotic as the doubling map itself.

No congruence helps. Taken mod N, both branches are always possible, so the reachable residues fill everything: the search over the whole phase map mod N (N ≤ 48, and 64 to 256) always reaches a fatal residue, and in the coordinates (s, L) the two branches reach every pair of the right parity mod every N ≤ 64. What decides the halt is the size of s, not a residue. The crude model (s uniform on the circle) predicts about ½ ln L midpoint all-ones tapes up to modulus L, 7.1 in the first 20,000,000 phases against 10 seen, and a chance below 10−10 of a fatal one after the 1011 phases already run.

sections.heading: The phase map in Lean
html: Every configuration the run passes through at a phase boundary is one of three shapes: E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, R(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y C>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, k, t) = (10)^m 1 A>0 0 (10)^k 1^t. The function next in lean/Phases.lean sends each one to the next shape the machine reaches, and next_sound proves each of its 18 cases for all parameters, from symbolic runs generated by py/pieces.py. Nothing is left out: next is undefined only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), and those halt.

So the question is exactly whether the orbit of R(0, 2), which the blank tape reaches in 2 steps, under next reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1) (halts_iff). The first 108 iterates do not (native_decide); by the step counts that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps. The even phases cannot reach a halt without an all-ones tape in between, and for all-ones tapes shorter than 105 cells Lean checks which ones lead to a halt first: n = 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …). lean/Fatal.lean proves that list for every n. lean/Ones.lean puts the pieces together (halt_needs_ones): the machine halts if and only if its run reaches an all-ones tape of fatal length. The last open step is to show that the run never hits one.

python3 py/rules.py reads the cases and their step counts from the Lean files and checks them against py/phasemap.py and against direct simulation: all 17 cases on 891 phases (every variable below 9), every row of the table on 4,262 instances (variables below 12), and every phase of the first 3·107 steps from blank tape (1,877 phases), where the tapes agree and the step counts add up.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.334). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.342).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,148 cells (1,697 left of the start, 1,676 right), with a density of 1s of 0.906.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Two blocks, (10)^x and 1^y, take turns doubling at each other's expense; Lean proves it halts if and only if an all-ones tape 1^n ever has n = 32·2^k − 2k − 12 (or one of a few values below 40), and that has not happened. Accelerated run: no halt in 8.16e23 steps.
